subject: Art & Design
title: Kerning: The Space Between Letters
description: Learn Kerning: The Space Between Letters in one minute.

hook.text: Look at the word 'WAVE.' The space between W and A feels wider than between A and V. That's a kerning problem.

buildup.text: Kerning is adjusting the space between individual letter pairs so spacing looks visually even.

discovery.text: Optical spacing ≠ mathematical spacing. Diagonal letters (A, V, W) need tighter gaps to look right.

twist.text: Bad kerning can be disastrous: 'click' can look like a very different word with poor letter spacing.

climax.text: Professional fonts include kerning tables — pre-set adjustments for hundreds of letter pairs.

punchline.text: Good kerning is invisible. Bad kerning is unforgettable.

quiz.question: What is kerning?
options: Adjusting space between individual letter pairs

details.summary: Kerning adjusts the spacing between specific letter pairs to achieve visually even spacing. Without kerning, certain pairs — AV, To, WA — appear to have gaps because their shapes don't fit snugly. Good kerning is invisible; bad kerning makes words look awkward and amateurish.
details.whyItMatters: Kerning is one of the most visible signs of typographic quality. Poorly kerned headlines distract readers and signal a lack of attention to detail. Professional designers obsess over kerning because it separates polished work from amateur design.
takeaways: Kerning adjusts spacing between specific letter pairs
Pairs like AV and To need manual adjustment for evenness
Good kerning is invisible; bad kerning looks amateurish

faq.question: What is the difference between kerning and tracking?
faq.answer: Kerning adjusts spacing between specific pairs of letters for optical evenness. Tracking adjusts spacing uniformly across an entire word or text block. Kerning is surgical (fix the AV gap); tracking is global (add breathing room to a headline). Both affect spacing but serve different purposes.

faq.question: Do you need to kern body text?
faq.answer: Rarely. Quality fonts include built-in kerning tables with hundreds of pair adjustments. At small sizes, kerning issues are barely visible. Manual kerning matters most for large headlines, logos, and display type where spacing imperfections become obvious and glaring.
